stem: Light year is a unit of
solution:
A light year is the distance travelled by light in one year.
\(1\ \text{ly} = c\,t = (3 \times 10^{8}\,\text{m s}^{-1})(3.16 \times 10^{7}\,\text{s}) \approx 9.46 \times 10^{15}\,\text{m}\).
The word 'year' names the time used inside that product, not the quantity the unit measures.
Matches option C.

stem: Which of the following is not equal to watt
solution:
A watt is \(1\,\text{J s}^{-1}\).
\(\text{ampere} \times \text{volt} = \text{A} \times \text{J C}^{-1} = \text{J s}^{-1}\), a watt.
\((\text{ampere})^{2} \times \text{ohm} = I^{2}R\), which is power, a watt.
\(\dfrac{\text{ampere}}{\text{volt}} = \dfrac{1}{\text{ohm}}\), the siemens, which measures conductance and not power.
Matches option D.

stem: One nanometre is equal to
solution:
\(1\,\text{nm} = 10^{-9}\,\text{m}\).
\(1\,\text{m} = 10^{2}\,\text{cm}\), so \(10^{-9}\,\text{m} = 10^{-9} \times 10^{2}\,\text{cm} = 10^{-7}\,\text{cm}\).
Testing the rest: \(10^{-6}\,\text{cm} = 10^{-8}\,\text{m}\) and \(10^{-9}\,\text{cm} = 10^{-11}\,\text{m}\), each off by a power of ten, while \(10^{9}\,\text{mm} = 10^{6}\,\text{m}\).
Matches option C.
reviewNote: Printed defect, already recorded in the note, and it does NOT disturb the key. Option (a) prints \(10^{9}\,\text{mm}\) with no minus sign, i.e. \(10^{6}\,\text{m}\), which is \(10^{15}\) times 1 nm. Worth recording: even the usual printed form of that distractor, \(10^{-9}\,\text{mm}\), does not equal 1 nm either, since \(1\,\text{nm} = 10^{-6}\,\text{mm}\). Either reading leaves \(10^{-7}\,\text{cm}\) as the single correct value, so exactly one option is right and the OMR key is safe.

stem: In \(S = a + bt + ct^{2}\). \(S\) is measured in metres and \(t\) in seconds. The unit of \(c\) is
solution:
Given \(S = a + bt + ct^{2}\), with \(S\) in metres and \(t\) in seconds.
Only like quantities may be added, so every term must carry the unit of \(S\): \([ct^{2}] = m\).
\([c] = \dfrac{m}{s^{2}} = ms^{-2}\).
Matches option D.

stem: Density of wood is \(0.5\,gm/cc\) in the CGS system of units. The corresponding value in MKS units is
solution:
Given \(\rho = 0.5\,\text{g cm}^{-3}\).
\(1\,\text{g} = 10^{-3}\,\text{kg}\) and \(1\,\text{cm}^{3} = 10^{-6}\,\text{m}^{3}\).
\(\rho = 0.5 \times \dfrac{10^{-3}\,\text{kg}}{10^{-6}\,\text{m}^{3}} = 0.5 \times 10^{3}\,\text{kg m}^{-3}\).
\(= 500\,\text{kg m}^{-3}\), so the magnitude in MKS units is 500.
Matches option A.

stem: One Mach number is equal to
solution:
Mach number is defined as \(M = \dfrac{\text{speed of the body}}{\text{speed of sound in the medium}}\).
Putting \(M = 1\) makes the speed of the body equal to the speed of sound.
In air that is about \(332\,\text{m s}^{-1}\).
Matches option B.

stem: If the unit of length and force be increased four times, then the unit of energy is
solution:
Energy is force times displacement, so \([E] = [F][L]\).
Making the unit of force 4 times larger and the unit of length 4 times larger multiplies the unit of energy by \(4 \times 4\).
\(= 16\) times.
Matches option C.

stem: Parsec is a unit of
solution:
A parsec is the distance at which one astronomical unit subtends a parallax angle of one arcsecond.
\(1\,\text{parsec} = 3.26\ \text{light years} \approx 3.09 \times 10^{16}\,\text{m}\).
The 'sec' in the name is the arcsecond of angle used to define it, not a time.
Matches option A.

\(1\,\text{kWh}\) is the energy delivered by a power of \(1\,\text{kW}\) acting for one hour.
\(E = Pt = (10^{3}\,\text{W}) \times (3600\,\text{s})\).
\(= 3.6 \times 10^{6}\,\text{J} = 36 \times 10^{5}\,\text{J}\).
Matches option B.

stem: Which relation is wrong
solution:
The question asks which relation is wrong, so each is tested in turn.
\(1\ \text{calorie} = 4.18\,\text{J}\) is correct.
\(1\,\text{\AA} = 10^{-10}\,\text{m}\) is correct.
\(1\,\text{MeV} = 10^{6} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\,\text{J} = 1.6 \times 10^{-13}\,\text{J}\) is correct.
\(1\,\text{N} = 1\,\text{kg m s}^{-2} = (10^{3}\,\text{g})(10^{2}\,\text{cm s}^{-2}) = 10^{5}\,\text{dyne}\), so the printed \(10^{-5}\,\text{dyne}\) is wrong by a factor \(10^{10}\).
Matches option D.

stem: The equation \(\left(P + \frac{a}{V^{2}}\right)(V - b)\) constant. The units of \(a\) are
solution:
In \(\left(P + \dfrac{a}{V^{2}}\right)\), only like quantities may be added, so \(\dfrac{a}{V^{2}}\) must have the units of pressure.
\([a] = [P][V^{2}]\).
In the CGS system \([P] = \text{dyne cm}^{-2}\) and \([V^{2}] = \text{cm}^{6}\).
\([a] = \text{dyne cm}^{-2} \times \text{cm}^{6} = \text{dyne} \times \text{cm}^{4}\).
Matches option B.
reviewNote: Printed defect already recorded in the note: the stem omits the '=' before 'constant'. The key is unaffected, because the units of \(a\) follow from the addition \(P + a/V^{2}\) alone and never from the right-hand side. Cross-checked against the same physics stated dimensionally, where \([a] = ML^{5}T^{-2}\); that is the same claim as dyne \(\times\) cm\(^{4}\), since \(\text{dyne} = \text{g cm s}^{-2}\).

stem: The correct value of \(0^{\circ}C\) on the Kelvin scale is
solution:
The Kelvin and Celsius scales are related by \(T = t + 273.15\).
At \(t = 0^{\circ}C\), \(T = 0 + 273.15 = 273.15\,\text{K}\).
The question asks for the correct value, so the rounded figures \(273\,\text{K}\) and \(273.2\,\text{K}\) do not qualify, and \(272.85\,\text{K}\) would correspond to \(-0.3^{\circ}C\).
Matches option A.

stem: In C.G.S. system the magnitude of the force is 100 dynes. In another system where the fundamental physical quantities are kilogram, metre and minute, the magnitude of the force is
solution:
Force has dimensions \(MLT^{-2}\), so \(n_{2} = n_{1}\left(\dfrac{M_{1}}{M_{2}}\right)\left(\dfrac{L_{1}}{L_{2}}\right)\left(\dfrac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}\right)^{-2}\).
\(\dfrac{M_{1}}{M_{2}} = \dfrac{\text{g}}{\text{kg}} = 10^{-3}\), \(\dfrac{L_{1}}{L_{2}} = \dfrac{\text{cm}}{\text{m}} = 10^{-2}\), \(\dfrac{T_{1}}{T_{2}} = \dfrac{\text{s}}{60\,\text{s}} = \dfrac{1}{60}\).
\(n_{2} = 100 \times 10^{-3} \times 10^{-2} \times 60^{2} = 100 \times 10^{-5} \times 3600\).
\(= 3.6\).
Check by a second route: \(100\,\text{dyne} = 10^{-3}\,\text{N} = 10^{-3}\,\text{kg m s}^{-2}\), and one minute squared is \(3600\,\text{s}^{2}\), giving \(10^{-3} \times 3600 = 3.6\).
Matches option C.

stem: Dimensional formula \(ML^{2}T^{-3}\) represents
solution:
Power is work per unit time, so \([\text{power}] = \dfrac{ML^{2}T^{-2}}{T} = ML^{2}T^{-3}\).
Work and energy are both \(ML^{2}T^{-2}\), and force is \(MLT^{-2}\).
Only power carries \(T^{-3}\), so it is the quantity the printed formula represents.
Matches option B.

stem: The dimensions of universal gravitational constant are

The frequency of vibration \(f\) of a mass \(m\) suspended from a spring of spring constant \(K\) is given by a relation of this type \(f = C\,m^{x}K^{y}\); where \(C\) is a dimensionless quantity. The value of \(x\) and \(y\) are
solution:
Given \(f = C\,m^{x}K^{y}\) with \(C\) dimensionless.
\([f] = T^{-1}\), \([m] = M\), and \([K] = \dfrac{\text{force}}{\text{length}} = \dfrac{MLT^{-2}}{L} = MT^{-2}\).
\(T^{-1} = M^{x}\left(MT^{-2}\right)^{y} = M^{x+y}T^{-2y}\).
Comparing powers of \(T\): \(-2y = -1\), so \(y = \dfrac{1}{2}\).
Comparing powers of \(M\): \(x + y = 0\), so \(x = -\dfrac{1}{2}\).
This reproduces the standard result \(f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{K}{m}}\).
Matches option D.

stem: \(MLT^{-1}\) represents the dimensional formula of
solution:
Momentum is \(p = mv\), so \([p] = M \times LT^{-1} = MLT^{-1}\).
Force is \(MLT^{-2}\), a couple is \(ML^{2}T^{-2}\), and power is \(ML^{2}T^{-3}\).
Only momentum carries \(MLT^{-1}\).
Matches option B.

stem: The velocity of a freely falling body changes as \(g^{p}h^{q}\) where g is acceleration due to gravity and \(h\) is the height. The values of \(p\) and \(q\) are
solution:
Given \(v \propto g^{p}h^{q}\).
\(LT^{-1} = (LT^{-2})^{p}(L)^{q} = L^{p+q}T^{-2p}\).
Comparing powers of \(T\): \(-2p = -1\), so \(p = \dfrac{1}{2}\).
Comparing powers of \(L\): \(p + q = 1\), so \(q = \dfrac{1}{2}\).
The familiar result \(v = \sqrt{2gh}\) carries the same two half powers.
Matches option B.

stem: The dimensions of pressure is equal to
solution:
\([\text{pressure}] = \dfrac{\text{force}}{\text{area}} = \dfrac{MLT^{-2}}{L^{2}} = ML^{-1}T^{-2}\).
\(\dfrac{\text{energy}}{\text{volume}} = \dfrac{ML^{2}T^{-2}}{L^{3}} = ML^{-1}T^{-2}\), which is the same.
\(\dfrac{\text{force}}{\text{volume}} = \dfrac{MLT^{-2}}{L^{3}} = ML^{-2}T^{-2}\), one power of length short.
Force and energy taken alone carry no negative power of length at all.
Matches option B.

stem: Density of a liquid in CGS system is \(0.625\,g/cm^{3}\). What is its magnitude in SI system
solution:
Given \(\rho = 0.625\,\text{g cm}^{-3}\).
\(\rho = 0.625 \times \dfrac{10^{-3}\,\text{kg}}{10^{-6}\,\text{m}^{3}} = 0.625 \times 10^{3}\,\text{kg m}^{-3}\).
\(= 625\,\text{kg m}^{-3}\), so the magnitude in SI units is 625.
Matches option D.

stem: The percentage errors in the measurement of mass and speed are 2% and 3% respectively. How much will be the maximum error in the estimation of the kinetic energy obtained by measuring mass and speed
solution:
\(E = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}\).
For a product of powers the maximum fractional error is the sum of the fractional errors, each weighted by its power: \(\dfrac{\Delta E}{E} = \dfrac{\Delta m}{m} + 2\dfrac{\Delta v}{v}\).
\(= 2\% + 2(3\%) = 2\% + 6\%\).
\(= 8\%\).
Matches option B.

stem: What is the number of significant figures in \(0.310 \times 10^{3}\)
solution:
In \(0.310 \times 10^{3}\) the power of ten is only a scale factor, so the significant figures are those of \(0.310\).
A leading zero placed before the first non-zero digit is not significant, but a trailing zero to the right of the decimal point is.
The significant digits are \(3, 1, 0\), so there are 3 of them.
Matches option B.

stem: Error in the measurement of radius of a sphere is 1%. The error in the calculated value of its volume is
solution:
\(V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}\), so \(V \propto r^{3}\).
\(\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} = 3\dfrac{\Delta r}{r}\).
\(= 3 \times 1\% = 3\%\).
Matches option B.

stem: A body travels uniformly a distance of \((13.8 \pm 0.2)\,m\) in a time \((4.0 \pm 0.3)\) s. The velocity of the body within error limits is
solution:
\(v = \dfrac{s}{t} = \dfrac{13.8}{4.0} = 3.45\,\text{m s}^{-1}\).
For a quotient the fractional errors add: \(\dfrac{\Delta v}{v} = \dfrac{\Delta s}{s} + \dfrac{\Delta t}{t}\).
\(= \dfrac{0.2}{13.8} + \dfrac{0.3}{4.0} = 0.0145 + 0.0750 = 0.0895\).
\(\Delta v = 3.45 \times 0.0895 = 0.309\), which to one decimal place is \(0.3\,\text{m s}^{-1}\).
\(v = (3.45 \pm 0.3)\,\text{m s}^{-1}\).
Matches option B.

stem: The decimal equivalent of 1/20 upto three significant figures is
solution:
\(\dfrac{1}{20} = 0.05\).
Leading zeros are not significant, so \(0.05\) as written shows only one significant figure.
To show three, two further zeros are written after the 5: \(0.0500\).
Of the rest, \(0.05000\) shows four significant figures, \(5.0 \times 10^{-2}\) shows two, and \(0.0050\) is a different number altogether.
Matches option A.

stem: The resistance \(R = \frac{V}{i}\) where \(V = 100 \pm 5\ volts\) and \(i = 10 \pm 0.2\ amperes\). What is the total error in \(R\)
solution:
\(R = \dfrac{V}{i}\), and for a quotient the fractional errors add: \(\dfrac{\Delta R}{R} = \dfrac{\Delta V}{V} + \dfrac{\Delta i}{i}\).
\(= \dfrac{5}{100} + \dfrac{0.2}{10} = 0.05 + 0.02\).
\(= 0.07 = 7\%\).
Matches option B.

stem: The period of oscillation of a simple pendulum in the experiment is recorded as 2.63 s, 2.56 s, 2.42 s, 2.71 s and 2.80 s respectively. The average absolute error is
solution:
Mean value \(\bar{T} = \dfrac{2.63 + 2.56 + 2.42 + 2.71 + 2.80}{5} = \dfrac{13.12}{5} = 2.624\,\text{s}\).
Absolute errors, each \(\left|T_{i} - \bar{T}\right|\): \(0.006,\ 0.064,\ 0.204,\ 0.086,\ 0.176\).
Their sum is \(0.536\).
Mean absolute error \(= \dfrac{0.536}{5} = 0.1072\,\text{s}\), which to two decimal places is \(0.11\,\text{s}\).
Matches option B.

stem: If 97.52 is divided by 2.54, the correct result in terms of significant figures is
solution:
\(\dfrac{97.52}{2.54} = 38.3937\ldots\)
In multiplication and division the result keeps as many significant figures as the least precise datum.
\(97.52\) carries four significant figures and \(2.54\) carries three, so the quotient keeps three.
Rounding \(38.3937\) to three significant figures gives \(38.4\).
Matches option A.

stem:
Assertion: Force can be added to pressure.
Reason: Force and pressure have same dimensions.
optA: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion
optB: Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion
optC: Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect
optD: Both Assertion and Reason are incorrect
solution:
Testing the Reason first: \([\text{force}] = MLT^{-2}\), while \([\text{pressure}] = \dfrac{MLT^{-2}}{L^{2}} = ML^{-1}T^{-2}\).
The two differ by a factor \(L^{2}\), so force and pressure do not have the same dimensions and the Reason is false.
Only quantities of identical dimensions may be added, so force cannot be added to pressure and the Assertion is false too.
Both statements are therefore incorrect.
Matches option D.

stem:
Match the following

| Column I | Column II |
|---|---|
| A. Random error | I. Ratio of mean absolute error to the mean value. |
| B. Absolute error | II. Relative error expressed in percentage. |
| C. Percentage error | III. Occurs due to unpredictable fluctuations in experimental conditions. |
| D. Relative error | IV. Difference between the individual measurement value and true value. |

Select the correct answer from the option given below.
solution:
Random error is the one that arises from unpredictable fluctuations in the experimental conditions, so it pairs with III.
Absolute error is the magnitude of the difference between an individual measurement and the true value, so it pairs with IV.
Percentage error is the relative error expressed in percentage, so it pairs with II.
Relative error is the ratio of the mean absolute error to the mean value, so it pairs with I.
Reading the four rows of Column I in the order the table prints them, the pairing runs III, IV, II, I.
Matches option A.
